economic_intuition: Higher sales per employee reflects improved labor-force productivity or restructuring efficiency, but the paper reports weaker/exceptional evidence for LF than for several other signals.
detailed_definition: Paper LF signal: change in sales per employee relative to the prior two-year average of sales per employee.

implied_factor_direction.note: The paper reports an explicit regression-weighted zero-investment strategy, not a simple high-minus-low or low-minus-high spread. Individual decile high/low legs are not the main specification.

comparison_policy.note: Do not compare this paper main specification to a simple high-minus-low sorted spread without a separate normalizer decision; the paper main specification uses regression-weighted zero-investment portfolios.

input_return.name: size_adjusted_buy_and_hold_abnormal_return
input_return.benchmark: daily compounded return of the value-weighted firm-size decile to which the security belongs over the same period

source.location: Section III Methodology, Data and Sample Selection p.27; Equation (2)
source.quote: "compound the daily returns"; "BHAR(+m)it = Π(1 + Rij) - Π(1 + SARkj)"
source.interpretation: The paper computes firm-level buy-and-hold abnormal returns from daily compounded security returns minus daily compounded size-decile benchmark returns. Paper return expression: BHAR(+m)_{it} = Π_{j=1}^{M}(1 + R_{ij}) - Π_{j=1}^{M}(1 + SAR_{kj}) Input-return components: R_i_j: daily return for security i on day j; SAR_k_j: daily return for the value-weighted firm-size decile k to which security i belongs on day j Cumulation window: {"start": "fourth_month_after_fiscal_year_end_t", "end": "through_m_subsequent_months; daily returns are cumulated through the third month of the following year for the annual window"}

adjustments.description: For firms that delist during the cumulation period, include the delisting return and then reinvest remaining-period returns in the firm's size-portfolio benchmark, implying zero abnormal returns for the remainder of the year.

source.location: Section III Methodology, Data and Sample Selection p.28; Footnote 9 context
source.quote: "For firms that delist, we include the delisting return"; "thereafter, the returns for the firm are reinvested in the size portfolio"
source.interpretation: This is an explicit paper rule for constructing firm-level BHAR after delisting, and should be represented in the return-calculation layer rather than only as a sample-coverage note.

return_combination.expression: return is the regression-weighted zero-investment portfolio return associated with this signal-specific regression regressor
return_combination.note: The aggregate paper strategy sums coefficients across signals, but this individual factor JSON records only the signal-specific portfolio return.

regression.equation: BHAR(+m)_it = a0 + Σ_k a_k RSIGNAL_k,it + a10 RBETA_it + a11 RCEPS_it + e_it

source.location: Section III Methodology, Hedge Portfolio Construction pp.25-27; Section IV Empirical Results pp.28-31; Equation (1)
source.quote: "Panel B of table 2 reports the mean regression coefficients"; "An individual coefficient represents the abnormal return to a zero-investment portfolio"
source.interpretation: The individual factor portfolio return is the regression coefficient associated with this signal-specific regressor. Continuous signals are scaled decile ranks; AQ and EQ retain zero/one values. The firm-level input return is size-adjusted BHAR.

portfolio_return.interpretation: For paper variable LF, the regression uses the scaled decile-rank version of the signal (for example, LF is converted to RLF after annual decile ranking and scaling to [0,1]). The coefficient on that ranked signal regressor is interpreted as the return to this signal-specific zero-investment factor portfolio.
